newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares off earlier highs in late IBIS trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares off earlier highs in late IBIS trade.

text.p: German shares settled off earlier highs in afternoon electronic trade on the IBIS DAX index, boosted mainly by ongoing dollar strength and firm Bunds and futures, but dealers described the trade as nervous.
At 1455 GMT the IBIS DAX stood at 3,207.40 points, up 15.95 points, off an earlier record high of 3,239.29 points, but above the psychologically-important 3,200-point threshold.

"It's the dollar again, and the Bunds, which everyone is watching. There a couple of decent features to this market, but it needs a good consolidation and trade seems nervous at the moment," said one trader.
American investment houses Morgan Stanley, Salomon Brothers and Merrill Lynch all cut their first quarter earnings per share (EPS) outlooks on IBM earlier in the day.
This contributed to market jitters, as traders feared a correction on Wall Street early on.
In the end, the Dow Jones Industrial index opened stronger, up 0.37 percent at 6,883.51 points early on, but the nervousness was indicative of market vertigo at these levels.
Chemical stocks were among the favourites over the course of trade, but by late afternoon were trading off earlier highs amid profit-taking following the sector's good run.
BASF AG stood at 63.02 marks, up 12 pfennigs, Bayer AG was up 68 pfennigs 67.60 marks and Hoechst AG was up 55 pfennigs at 75.50 marks.
